table.name: badges
table.purpose: One row per badge awarded to a user on a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site (Stack Exchange 'Badges' export). Each row records a single badge (name) granted to a specific user at a specific date/time. A user can earn the same badge multiple times (e.g. tag-based badges).

col_001.name: badge_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Unique surrogate identifier for each badge award row. The many 'referenced_by' joins are spurious: other tables contain user/post ids that happen to fall in the same numeric range, not references to badge ids.

col_002.name: user_id
col_002.description: Id of the user who received the badge. References users.col_001 (many badges per user; ~25k distinct users among ~80k badges). The join to postHistory.col_001 is coincidental (both are user ids).

col_003.name: badge_name
col_003.description: Name of the badge awarded. Mostly standard Stack Exchange badge names (Student, Supporter, Editor, Scholar, Teacher, Autobiographer, Analytical, ...), plus tag-based badges whose name is a tag (e.g. 'correlation', 'pca', 'modeling', 'nonparametric', 'Outspoken') earned for activity in that tag.

col_004.name: awarded_at
col_004.description: Timestamp (date and time) when the badge was awarded, ranging from 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14.

table.name: comments
table.purpose: Comments on posts (StackExchange-style data dump): one row per comment made on a question or answer, with its text, score, author, and creation date.

col_001.name: comment_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the comment.

col_002.name: post_id
col_002.description: ID of the post (question or answer) the comment was made on; references posts.col_001.

col_003.name: score
col_003.description: Net vote score of the comment (upvotes minus downvotes); heavily skewed toward 0, max 90.

col_005.name: creation_date
col_005.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

col_006.name: user_id
col_006.description: ID of the user who wrote the comment; references users.col_001. Null for a small fraction (comments by deleted/anonymous users).

col_007.name: user_display_name
col_007.description: Display name of the comment author, populated only when the user record is missing/deleted (98.4% null); values like 'user10525' are typical of deleted accounts.

table.name: postHistory
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style post revision history: one row per edit/revision event on a post (initial creation, edits, closures, etc.).

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of the history event; unique integer.

col_002.name: postHistoryTypeId
col_002.description: Type of history event (revision type code). 25 distinct small codes; values 1-5 dominate (initial question/answer creation, edits). Exact code meanings not verifiable from data alone.

col_003.name: postId
col_003.description: Id of the post this history event belongs to; references posts.

col_004.name: revisionGuid
col_004.description: UUID grouping related history events into one revision (e.g. title/body/tag edits of the same revision share a GUID). All-zero GUID appears for system events.

col_005.name: creationDate
col_005.description: Timestamp when the history event occurred.

col_006.name: userId
col_006.description: Id of the user who caused the event; references users. -1 denotes the system/community user; null when the user was deleted/unknown.

col_007.name: text
col_007.description: Snapshot of the post content (body, title, or tags) at this revision; contains tag strings like <r>, post bodies, and JSON close-voter data depending on event type. Empty when not applicable.

col_008.name: comment
col_008.description: Editor's comment describing the change ('edited title', 'added 1 characters in body', 'removed signature and greetings'). Empty for most events.

col_009.name: userDisplayName
col_009.description: Display name of the user when no account id is available (e.g. deleted users, shown as 'userNNNNN'). Empty otherwise.

table.name: postLinks
table.purpose: Stack Overflow-style PostLinks table: each row records a link between two posts, either a related link or a duplicate-of link (LinkTypeId 1 = linked/related, 3 = duplicate).

col_001.name: Id
col_001.description: Primary key of the post link row; unique integer identifier.

col_002.name: CreationDate
col_002.description: Timestamp when the link was created.

col_003.name: PostId
col_003.description: Id of the post on which the link is recorded (references posts.Id).

col_004.name: RelatedPostId
col_004.description: Id of the post being linked to (references posts.Id); e.g. the duplicate target or related post.

col_005.name: LinkTypeId
col_005.description: Link type code: 1 = linked/related post (10186 rows), 3 = duplicate (916 rows). The joins to badges/comments/postHistory are spurious statistical matches, not real references.

table.name: posts
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style Q&A posts (questions and answers, apparently from Cross Validated / stats.stackexchange.com given the statistics-related content). One row per post; questions and answers share this table, distinguished by post type.

col_001.name: PostId
col_001.description: Primary key of the post. Referenced by comments, postHistory, votes, postLinks, tags.

col_002.name: PostTypeId
col_002.description: Post type code: 1 = question (42,912 rows), 2 = answer (47,755 rows); rarer values (3-7) likely wiki/moderation post types (e.g. tag wiki, moderator nomination).

col_003.name: AcceptedAnswerId
col_003.description: Id of the answer accepted as the solution; set only on questions that have an accepted answer (null 84% of rows). Values fall within the post-id range.

col_004.name: CreationDate
col_004.description: Timestamp when the post was created (2009-2014).

col_005.name: Score
col_005.description: Net vote score of the post (upvotes minus downvotes); can be negative (min -19).

col_006.name: ViewCount
col_006.description: Number of views; populated only for questions (null for answers, 53% null).

col_007.name: Body
col_007.description: Post body in HTML (questions and answers).

col_008.name: OwnerUserId
col_008.description: Id of the user who created the post; -1 denotes a system/community user. References users.

col_009.name: LastActivityDate
col_009.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity on the post (edit, answer, comment); never null and always >= creation date.

col_010.name: Title
col_010.description: Post title; populated only for questions (null for answers).

col_011.name: Tags
col_011.description: Angle-bracket-delimited tag list, e.g. <regression><r>; populated only for questions.

col_012.name: AnswerCount
col_012.description: Number of answers to the question; populated only for questions.

col_013.name: CommentCount
col_013.description: Number of comments on the post; never null, applies to both questions and answers.

col_014.name: FavoriteCount
col_014.description: Number of users who favorited/starred the post; populated only for questions (86% null).

col_015.name: LastEditorUserId
col_015.description: Id of the user who last edited the post (-1 = community user); null when never edited. References users.

col_016.name: LastEditDate
col_016.description: Timestamp of the last edit; null when the post was never edited (51% null).

col_017.name: ClosedDate
col_017.description: Timestamp when the post was closed (off-topic/duplicate etc.); null for the 97% of posts not closed.

col_018.name: ParentId
col_018.description: For answers, the Id of the parent question; null for questions (48% null, matching the answer share).

col_019.name: CommunityOwnedDate
col_019.description: Date the post became community wiki (no longer attributed to a single owner); null for 98% of posts.

col_020.name: OwnerDisplayName
col_020.description: Display name of the post owner when no user account is attached (e.g. 'user28'); mostly null.

col_021.name: LastEditorDisplayName
col_021.description: Display name of the last editor when no user account is attached; almost always null.

table.name: tags
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style tag directory (likely Cross Validated/stats site): one row per tag used on posts, with its usage count and links to the tag's excerpt and wiki posts in the posts table.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the tag.

col_003.name: count
col_003.description: Number of times the tag is used (usage count). Values are small positive integers with a long right tail (max 7244), consistent with counts, not a foreign key despite the accepted joins.

col_004.name: excerpt_post_id
col_004.description: Id of the post (posts.col_001) containing the tag's short excerpt/description; null when no excerpt exists. The one_to_one join to posts supports this.

col_005.name: wiki_post_id
col_005.description: Id of the post (posts.col_001) containing the tag's full wiki; null when none. Pairs with col_004 (excerpt), each typically one less than the other, matching Stack Exchange's ExcerptPostId/WikiPostId pattern.

table.name: users
table.purpose: Registered user accounts of a Stack Overflow-style Q&A site (one row per user), with profile data and per-user activity counters.

col_001.name: Id
col_001.description: Primary key: unique user id. Value -1 appears once, likely the system/community placeholder user. Referenced by badges, comments, postHistory and posts (author/owner).

col_002.name: AccountId
col_002.description: Global network account id linking this site user to a cross-site account (many users share id 1/101, the default for unlinked accounts). Not a key of this table.

col_003.name: CreationDate
col_003.description: Timestamp when the account was created (2010-2014).

col_004.name: DisplayName
col_004.description: Public display name of the user; many auto-generated 'userNNNNN' names.

col_005.name: LastAccessDate
col_005.description: Timestamp of the user's last site access; always >= creation date.

col_006.name: WebsiteUrl
col_006.description: User's personal website URL from their profile; ~80% empty, placeholders like 'http://none'.

col_007.name: Location
col_007.description: Free-text location from the profile (city/country strings).

col_008.name: AboutMe
col_008.description: HTML 'about me' bio text from the profile; ~77% empty.

col_009.name: Views
col_009.description: Count of profile views; heavily zero-skewed. Could alternatively be another small counter, but profile views fits the Stack Exchange schema.

col_010.name: DownVotes
col_010.description: Number of downvotes cast by the user (mostly 0).

col_011.name: UpVotes
col_011.description: Number of upvotes cast by the user (mostly 0).

col_012.name: Reputation
col_012.description: Unique per user, range -1 to ~5M, matching Stack Exchange reputation scores; -1 for the placeholder user. Alternative: some other monotonically assigned score, but reputation fits best.

col_014.name: ProfileImageUrl
col_014.description: URL of the user's avatar image (gravatar/google/facebook); ~59% null, default identicon URL most common.

table.name: votes
table.purpose: Votes cast on posts (StackOverflow-style data dump): one row per vote, linking a voter to a post with a vote type code and date; includes bounty amounts for bounty-related votes.

col_001.name: vote_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the vote row.

col_002.name: post_id
col_002.description: Id of the post being voted on; references posts (also matches postHistory/badges ids, but posts is the intended target given the table's purpose).

col_003.name: vote_type_id
col_003.description: Vote type code (StackOverflow VoteTypes): 1=accepted answer, 2=upvote, 3=downvote, 5=favorite, 8=bounty close, 16=bookmark/edit etc. Distribution dominated by 2 (upvotes). Exact mapping beyond common values (1,2,3,5) is inferred from typical SE dump conventions.

col_004.name: creation_date
col_004.description: Date the vote was cast (date only, no time).

col_005.name: user_id
col_005.description: Id of the user who cast the vote; null for most rows (anonymous/undisclosed voters, typical of SE dumps where only favorites/bounties expose the user). No accepted join detected, but value range matches user ids.

col_006.name: bounty_amount
col_006.description: Bounty amount in reputation points (values 0-200, multiples of 25); populated only on bounty-related votes (~0.3% of rows).
